title: Semgrep detects unsafe-add-mask workflow command in 14 GitHub Actions workflow files
signature: unsafe add mask workflow command detected in github actions workflows|Configuration
root_cause: Semgrep rule 'yaml.github-actions.security.audit.unsafe-add-mask-workflow-command' flagged 14 occurrences of 'echo ::add-mask::' usage across 13 workflow files. The rule detects that if a workflow command stop marker is injected, the add-mask command can be bypassed, leaking secrets into logs. All findings relate to SCCACHE_AZURE_CONNECTION_STRING (12 files) and MCP_GATEWAY_API_KEY (2 files - ci-doctor-mq.lock.yml and ci-doctor.lock.yml). This is a deterministic configuration/security finding that requires replacing bare echo-based masking with a more secure mechanism.
reproduction_steps: Run: docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/src semgrep/semgrep semgrep scan --error -j 8 --config 'p/github-actions' .github/workflows/*
recommended_actions: Replace 'echo ::add-mask::${SECRET}' with a GitHub Actions environment file approach: add the secret to $GITHUB_ENV with masking, or use the actions/core::setSecret API
For SCCACHE_AZURE_CONNECTION_STRING: replace bare echo masking with a run step that uses 'echo ::add-mask::' wrapped in stop-commands protection or migrate to a dedicated secret masking step
For MCP_GATEWAY_API_KEY in ci-doctor workflows: apply the same fix
prevention_strategies: Add semgrep to pre-commit or PR CI checks so new workflow files with unsafe add-mask patterns are caught before merge. Document the correct masking pattern in workflow authoring guidelines.
historical_context: No prior occurrence of this exact pattern in the CI Doctor MQ database. This is the first recorded semgrep security scan failure.
